If active, it is closed once with reason terminated_unjudgeable_dut_output: its tags are flushed as open unknowns, pending live entries give pending_at_unjudgeable_row (K12 unresolved, not a batch-end activation), and slave-canceled ones are counted. rationale: Review N1/N2: the pd-only termination path broke out without flushing row-start tags or closing the epoch. As a result, possible_starvation_err and the pending entries were lost, and K6 was misreported as checked_not_refuted.
The repair closes the unchanged row-start H with a distinct termination reason. It is not labelled as reset, batch end or an env boundary, and the K10 failure and unjudgeable_row are kept.
Suspended and dead modes are untouched because close_epoch returns early, so there is no double flush and the discarded-evidence disclosure is preserved.

Four new selftests cover the retained tag, pending work, scope statuses, the distinct boundary fields, the unprocessed reset suffix and the clean-prefix case. All existing tests and limits are unchanged.
contract_decisions: Undefined DUT control output: dut_violation is retained. The valid-prefix snapshot unit is the history set at the start of the terminated row, and it is closed as terminated_unjudgeable_dut_output.
Pending work at termination is reported as pending_at_unjudgeable_row under K12 (unresolved). It is not counted as a K12 batch-end activation.
termination_boundary is kept separate from input_validity_boundary. Prefix qualification of clause statuses applies to both.
No timeout or cancellation semantics are added, no rule is weakened, and no freeze, replay or B/C is authorized.
